n`--case` accepts a hosted row id, which does not exist yet when this check\nruns. A selector this stage cannot map is therefore t

A selected `approximated` case refuses unless this invocation approves it:

| Flag | Required | Description |
\n| - | - | - |\n| `--allow-approximated <case...>` | No | Approve an `approximated` imported case for **this run only**, by AUTHO
RED case id (`cases[].id`). Repeatable. `--file` runs only |\n| `--approval-reason <text>` | With the above | Why the approximatio
ns are acceptable for this run. 1–500 characters after trimming; one reason covers every approval in the invocation |\n\n```bash t
heme={\"theme\":\"css-variables\"}\nmcpjam cloud eval run --file .mcpjam/evals/s_billing.yaml \\\n --allow-approximated c_refund_

partial \
 --approval-reason "Reviewed against the upstream rubric; ENG-4821"
```

Checked before anything is billed, each
with its own message: approving a\n**native** case (nothing to approve), a **claimed-exact** one (needs no\napproval), an **unsup
ported** or **unresolved** one (approval covers a case\nwhose behaviour was approximated, not one whose behaviour is missing), a\n
**disabled** or **unselected** one (the run will not execute it), an unknown\nid, or the same id twice. The flags are refused outr
ight with `--suite`: a\nhosted suite's cases are not the ones this invocation authored, so an\nauthored-id selector has nothing to

resolve against.

**The approval belongs to the run, never to the case.** You supply an id and a
reason and nothing else — the
approver and the timestamp are derived by the\nserver and frozen into that run's own snapshot, because a caller-supplied\napprove
r would file one person's approval under another's name and a\ncaller-supplied timestamp could be backdated past the edit that inv
alidated the\nclaim. Nothing persists: edit the suite, re-sync, or launch again, and the flags\nserver references or fixtures agai

nst a project's live discovery, so a file that
validates here can still fail to run.

inst a real project
